evidence: M-O s.v. chesspieces6: pawn, from Du Cange quoting Pseudo-Ovid, and Vida
terms.comment: The foot soldier (Caes., Liv.): the name of the piece since the Middle Ages, as English pawn comes from medieval Latin pedō, pedōnis, a foot soldier.

sources: Lewis & Short: pedes
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 52.
